the chemical composition and bioactivities of Cichoriam spinosum L., grown in nutrient solution containing different nitrate:ammonic ratio, are affected by the nitrogen source.

the modulation of the NO3 N:NHN4 N ratio in nutrient solution supplied to chicory plants can affect the chemical composition and the bioactive properties of the final product, thus enhancing the overall quality of chicory without compromising yield.
the chemical composition and bioactivity of C. spinosus are influenced by nitrate/ammonia nitrogen ratio in nutrient solutions.

the effects of nitrogen form and concentration in the nutrient solution on the chemical composition of C. spinosus, a vegetable with high potential for human health promotion.
the effects of different N sources and their ratios on chemical composition and biological properties of C. spinosus.
the effects of different nitrogenous fertilizers on the quality of C. spinosun leaves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nitrate:am monium nitrogen ratio in fertigation solution may affect chemical composition and bioacti ve properties of C. spinos um leaves.

a balanced ratio of NO3 N: NH4 N (25:75) in nutrient solution is recommended for C. spinosus production, since it enhances the nutritional and bioactive properties and does not negatively affect yield.

the application of a balanced ratio of nitrate and ammonium nitrogen (50:50 NO(3) N:NH4 (4) N) in the nutrient solution, would result in a product of superior quality, with a higher content of bioactive compounds (tocopherols, sugars, organic acids, phenolic compounds and fatty acids) and lower content of antinutinents (oxalic acid) compared with the control (100:0) or the other ratios tested.
